topics.title: Boat engines & spawning
topics.takeaway: Manual driver exit now stops the engine automatically. Driver death keeps it running and still prevents transport-boat spawning.
topics.caution: This engine change does not establish that every missing-spawn problem is resolved.

changes.summary: Manual driver exit now stops the engine automatically. Driver death keeps the engine running and can still deny spawning.
changes.before: Leaving the driver seat did not automatically stop the engine.
changes.after: Manual exit switches the engine off. Driver death in the seat leaves it running.

topics.overview: Leaving a transport boat’s driver seat now switches its engine off. Being killed in the seat leaves it running.
topics.context: Transport-boat spawning requires the engine to be off. The update distinguishes a driver leaving the seat from a driver being killed there.

baselines.title: Transport boat engine shutdown
baselines.summary: Manual driver exit switches the engine off. Driver death in the seat leaves it running, which prevents transport-boat spawning until it is switched off.

issues.title: Spawn choices and Commander abilities can disappear
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.7 fixes one Commander vehicle-order input case, not the wider missing-spawn replication problem. General closure remains unconfirmed.

topics.title: Fortification costs & limits
topics.takeaway: Level 1 defenses cost no Supplies; upgrades still do. Barbed Wire increased from two to three per Engineer, capped at 50 per side.
topics.caution: Free Level 1 construction does not remove upgrade costs or placement limits.

changes.summary: Level 1 construction stopped consuming Supplies; higher-level upgrades still require them.
changes.after: Level 1 construction costs no Supplies. Higher-level upgrades still require Supplies.

changes.summary: Barbed Wire increased from two to three placements per Engineer, with a limit of 50 per side.
changes.before: Two Barbed Wire placements per Engineer.
changes.after: Three per Engineer, capped at 50 per side.

topics.overview: Basic defenses no longer require Supplies to build. Engineers can also place more Barbed Wire.
topics.context: These changes affect the Supplies needed for Engineer-built defenses and the number of Barbed Wire placements allowed.

baselines.title: Engineer buildables & Barbed Wire
baselines.summary: Level 1 construction remains free of Supplies; upgrades still cost Supplies. Barbed Wire is now three per Engineer, capped at 50 per side.

topics.title: Redeploy timer change
topics.takeaway: The additional ten-second Redeploy punishment was removed; the normal deployment wait remains.
topics.caution: This change does not mean instant spawning or guarantee that a spawn point is available.

changes.summary: Removed the additional ten-second punishment for choosing Redeploy.
changes.before: Choosing Redeploy added a ten-second punishment.
changes.after: That extra punishment is removed. The normal deployment timer still applies.

topics.overview: Choosing Redeploy no longer adds an extra ten-second wait. The normal deployment timer still applies.
topics.context: The removed punishment was additional to the normal deployment timer.

baselines.title: Redeploy punishment timer
baselines.summary: Choosing Redeploy no longer adds a ten-second punishment; the normal deployment timer still applies.

topics.title: Tank ammunition changes
topics.takeaway: Selecting another shell type unloads the chambered round and automatically loads the chosen ammunition.
topics.caution: The notes establish unloading and reloading, not an instant ammunition swap.

changes.summary: Added shell unloading when changing ammunition types.
changes.before: The loaded round had to be fired before changing shell types.
changes.after: Changing type unloads the chambered round and automatically loads the selected type.

topics.overview: Tanks can now change their loaded ammunition type without firing the round already in the gun.
topics.context: The change concerns a round already loaded in the tank’s gun when a different ammunition type is selected.

baselines.title: Tank shell unloading
baselines.summary: Selecting another shell type unloads the chambered round and automatically loads the chosen type.

issues.title: Tank gunner seat changes silently switch ammunition to AP
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.7 fixes leaving or changing the Gunner seat switching ammunition to AP while the display still shows the previous shell.

topics.title: Medic & Rifleman slots
topics.takeaway: Medic slots increased from one to two per unit; Rifleman slots decreased from three to two.
topics.caution: Further Medic proposals are excluded from this released slot change.

changes.summary: Added a second Medic slot and reduced Rifleman slots from three to two.
changes.before: One Medic slot and three Rifleman slots per unit.
changes.after: Two Medic slots and two Rifleman slots per unit.

topics.overview: Each unit now has room for two Medics and two Riflemen, instead of one Medic and three Riflemen.
topics.context: The change reallocates the number of players who can hold each of these roles in a unit.

baselines.title: Unit composition & Medics
baselines.summary: Units have two Medic slots and two Rifleman slots, replacing one and three respectively.

topics.title: New US weapons & magazines
topics.takeaway: Selected US roles gained the M1A1 Thompson. The M16A1 now offers 30-round magazines alongside the 20-round option, with increased Weight costs.
topics.caution: Thompson access is role-specific. Exact role access and magazine Weight values are included in the current rules below.

changes.summary: Added the M1A1 Thompson to selected US roles and an optional 30-round M16A1 configuration.
changes.before: The listed US roles did not have the Thompson option. The existing M16A1 magazine option held 20 rounds.
changes.after: The Thompson is available to the listed US roles. M16A1 users can select 30-round magazines; the 20-round option remains.

topics.overview: Some US roles gained the Thompson submachine gun. The M16A1 gained an optional larger magazine.
topics.context: These are US loadout additions. The 20-round M16A1 configuration remains available.

baselines.title: M1A1 Thompson
baselines.summary: US access: Commander, Tank Commander, Crewman, Mortar Observer, Sniper, Squad Leader, Medic, Specialist, Grenadier and Engineer.

baselines.title: M16A1 30-round magazines
baselines.summary: Optional 30-round configuration: six magazines by default, up to ten via Barracks. The weapon gains one Weight; each magazine costs two Weight versus one for a 20-round magazine.

topics.title: Boat handling & Fuel costs
topics.takeaway: Both boats gained handling and top-speed improvements. The US PBR’s speed advantage increased; the NVA boat rose from 200 to 250 Fuel.
topics.caution: The notes describe relative handling and speed changes; exact speed and acceleration values are not supplied.

changes.summary: Improved both boats’ handling and top speed, increased the US PBR’s relative speed and acceleration advantage, and raised the NVA boat’s Fuel cost by 50.
changes.before: The NVA boat cost 200 Fuel. Earlier speed and handling values are not quantified in these notes.
changes.after: The NVA boat costs 250 Fuel. Both boats have improved handling and top speed, with a larger US PBR speed and acceleration advantage.

topics.overview: Both factions’ boats received handling and speed changes. The NVA boat also costs more Fuel.
topics.context: The release changes boat movement and the Fuel cost of the supply-carrying NVA boat.

baselines.title: Boat handling, speed & Fuel balance
baselines.summary: Both factions gain handling and top-speed improvements. The US PBR has a larger speed/acceleration advantage; the supply-carrying NVA boat now costs 250 Fuel, up from 200.

topics.title: Vehicle machine-gun resupply
topics.takeaway: Tank coaxial MGs and boat Machine Gunner positions can now be resupplied before their ammunition runs out.
topics.caution: Equal resupply of the two boat bow guns is a separate reported issue and is not explicitly confirmed fixed by this change.

changes.summary: Allowed ammunition top-ups before empty for tank coaxial MGs and boat Machine Gunner positions.
changes.before: These guns had to be completely empty before receiving more ammunition.
changes.after: They can receive ammunition while some rounds remain.

topics.overview: Some tank and boat machine guns can now receive more ammunition before they are completely empty.
topics.context: The update applies to tank coaxial machine guns and boat Machine Gunner positions.

baselines.title: Tank coaxial & boat MG ammunition top-ups
baselines.summary: Tank coaxial MGs and boat Machine Gunner positions can be resupplied before their ammunition is completely empty.

issues.title: Dual bow boat guns may reload only one weapon
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.7 permits boat-gun top-ups before empty. The separate report that only one dual bow gun reloads is not explicitly confirmed fixed.

topics.title: Controller Crouch / Melee swap
topics.takeaway: All controller layouts now offer a Crouch / Melee input swap.
topics.caution: Full controller remapping and a Radio / Equipment swap are not established by this release.

changes.summary: Released the Crouch / Melee input swap for controller layouts.
changes.before: The Crouch / Melee swap was a planned addition.
changes.after: The swap is available across all controller layouts.

topics.overview: Controller users gained an option to swap the Crouch and Melee inputs.
topics.context: This adds a specific two-input swap to the existing controller layouts.

baselines.title: Controller Crouch / Melee swap
baselines.summary: All controller layouts offer a Crouch / Melee input swap.

topics.title: Commander ability penalties
topics.takeaway: Team-kill punishment was removed for Commander abilities; personal weapons and other direct actions retain their usual punishment behavior.
topics.caution: This changes punishment for Commander abilities. It does not remove friendly fire or all penalties.

changes.summary: Removed Commander team-kill punishment for friendly deaths caused by abilities such as Napalm, Artillery Strikes and Bombing Runs.
changes.before: Friendly deaths from Commander abilities could add a team-kill punishment to the Commander.
changes.after: Those ability-related deaths no longer add that punishment. Personal weapons and other direct actions retain their usual punishment behavior.

topics.overview: Friendly deaths caused by Commander abilities no longer add the associated punishment to the Commander.
topics.context: The affected abilities include Napalm, Artillery Strikes and Bombing Runs.

baselines.title: Commander ability team-kill punishment
baselines.summary: Friendly deaths from Commander abilities such as Napalm, Artillery Strikes and Bombing Runs no longer add a team-kill punishment to the Commander.
